jobs.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: a mature Japanese science fiction mechanical design master sheet, FOUR independent spacecraft, large detailed landscape illustration. This is the single-craft design stage for a later monumental transforming fleet robot. Draw only the independent ships now, not any combined robot.

Input references and roles:
1 is the adopted museum ship. Preserve that ship's recognizable physical identity: its terraced ivory public decks, long blue window bands, glazed dome, orange entrance arch, broad forked bow promenade, lower navy structural hull, separate orange-capped engines, and short aft bridge.
2, 3 and 4 define the mature spacecraft design language: long coherent hulls, large angular armor planes, wedge bows, recessed hangars, functional thick skins and deep machinery. Do not copy their alternative designs or letters in the margins.
5 defines PAINTING DEPTH AND MECHANICAL VOLUME, not robot shapes to insert: powerful large planes, bevel thickness, layered dark occlusion between armor, selective exposed mechanical anatomy, subtle maintained paint wear, fine variable-weight drawing, convincing scale.

Layout: spacious two-by-two arrangement. Each entire ship isolated with generous cream background and no overlapping contours. All seen from the same elevated three-quarter front viewpoint, long hull axes diagonal across the sheet. Ships are shown at comparable page size for readability, not asserted to be the same real size. Tiny human/service-vehicle or shuttle scale cues may accompany each. No captions, names, numbers, logos, watermark, arrows or decorative diagram frames. Fill the sheet with detailed handsome ship portraits rather than making a grid of tiny icons.

Top left: the 150-meter museum cruise ship from reference 1, carefully retained, with its public architectural terraces, entrance arch and glass dome intact. The lower hull has real depth and substantial engines. The ship should still feel like a beloved mobile cultural building and a credible spacecraft, elegant and imposing rather than toy-like.

Top right: an independently propelled BRIDGE-RESCUE SHIP. A long, wide, armored bridge-ship with a heavy navy and ivory wedge prow and subtly blue-green identification panels. Large slanted flank plates enclose its massive load structure; bridge windows are narrow, human-scaled. Two deep protected buffered tow-drum recesses, stout docking collars along its flanks, and broad internal load decks establish its rescue role. Include a retracted armored bridging deck, not a naked crane scaffold. Its bow, stern engines and long hull must read as one complete ship, not a little tug. This craft will later support a damaged giant's left shoulder, but do not depict it connected now.

Bottom left: an independent MAINTENANCE CRUISER. A longer industrial ship with ivory and charcoal armor, a few muted ochre panels, and a compact asymmetrical bridge. A telescoping segmented coolant/service arm is nested along the lower-left side of its hull, with an articulated tool head, hose reel, protected maintenance galleries and worker access recesses. Large shell panels cover most of the chassis; intricate mechanisms are concentrated where they work. The arm can retract into the hull and the ship can leave independently. Make it handsome, heavy and coherent, not a floating toolbox.

Bottom right: a fast ESCORT GUNSHIP with broad folded wing-shields. Dark charcoal/navy with ivory armor and muted dark crimson panels, long sharp prow and muscular narrow waist, rear vector engines, integrated naval weapon batteries. Folded shield wings sweep along the hull as substantial angled armor, not solar panels. One isolated damaged side docking socket is visibly capped/under repair; it is NOT a load-bearing partner. It provides outboard covering fire and protects small evacuation craft. Keep the whole ship elongated and formidable; do not make a stubby service boat with a cannon pasted on it.

Art finish: closely match the sophisticated illustrated source art. Refined dark linework, large restrained color regions, dimensional chamfered plating, strongly recessed joints, layered local shading and restrained metallic edge highlights. Fine hatches, window rows and occasional paint wear provide scale without covering every surface. The primary silhouette must be striking and readable before the detail. No plastic toy gloss, no chibi rounding, no thick uniform cartoon outlines, no flat infographic simplification, no neon, no photorealistic PBR. Calm warm off-white studio background.

jobs.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: second spacecraft-and-dock-component master sheet for a monumental Japanese transforming fleet robot, in the SAME mature painted mechanical concept-art style as reference 1. These are the actual independent ships and large physical modules to be combined later. Draw the solo modules only. No assembled humanoid.

Reference roles:
1 is the new approved-for-this-proposal fleet master sheet: match the hull sophistication, narrow human-scale windows, coherent armor, fine dark drawing and deep shadowed industrial volumes. The museum and three support ships on that sheet are NOT to be redrawn here.
2 and 3 supply long military/industrial hull architecture, broad armor, recessed machinery, functional hangars.
4 and 5 supply powerful mechanical volume and mature surface treatment: large plated masses, deep joint cavities, legible panel thickness, restrained paint wear and layered shading. Do not insert their humanoids into this sheet.

Composition: a spacious detailed concept sheet with FIVE clearly separated groups. Top row: TWO large independent armored gun cruisers, one on each side. Middle row: ONE very large armored civilian orbital-dock carrier, spanning the width. Bottom left: a matching PAIR of long support-carrier ships. Bottom right: a matching PAIR of folded armored shoulder-boom/propulsion modules. Each entire object fully inside the canvas, clear gaps, no overlapping groups. Draw the spacecraft from elevated three-quarter front views with consistent lighting. Tiny shuttles and human service vehicles provide scale. These are NOT at a common physical scale on the page. No text, letters, numbers, arrows, emblems, watermarks, ornamental infographic borders or bright schematic color coding.

TOP LEFT: a formidable dark NAVY/IVORY gun cruiser. A long complete battleship hull, strong beveled wedge prow, broad almost unbroken angular armor planes, inset longitudinal gun galleries, recessed bridge slit and substantial aft engine group. Main weapons integrate with the hull's long axis rather than a single turret stuck on a tug. Two naval secondary batteries are small relative to its immense hull. A thick circular coupling collar is recessed into its aft underside, with mechanical load paths covered by armor. This ship will later form the UPPER part of a giant's right arm. It remains a credible independent cruiser now.

TOP RIGHT: a second true battleship with visibly DIFFERENT GRAY/DEEP CRIMSON paint. Similar physical mass and length to its navy companion but a sharper split prow, offset armored gun gallery, a distinct stepped aft bridge and stern engine geometry. Keep two large color regions, not multicolored patches. It will later form the FOREARM part of the right arm, end-to-end with the navy ship through a rotary elbow collar. Include a closed, heavily protected long loading/manipulator bay in its prow whose segmented armored door shape explains where the eventual hand can deploy from. No external humanoid fist in solo flight mode. Both cruisers must have impressive long ship silhouettes, thick armor and deep structure. They are not little orange harbor tugs.

MIDDLE: an imposing CIVILIAN ORBITAL-DOCK ARMOR CARRIER. A complete broad spacecraft/habitable dock with a thick central keel, handsome paired wedge-shaped hull masses, and large sloping ivory and navy armored shells. This is NOT a skeletal rectangle. Its enormous enclosed side-dock halls have tiny horizontal window strips, recessed passenger entrances and shuttered hangar mouths. Show one broad armored shutter slightly open to reveal a deep internal 150-meter-class ship cradle, with the lower exit route visible; do not place the museum ship inside now. The large paired outer shell panels have clear hinges, sliding tracks and a few small industrial yellow release levers. They can later close into a coherent hero's chest and shoulder armor, then be released as inhabited side-dock modules. Yellow locks are small mechanical latches, not flowers. The short central command bridge is deeply inset between two armored cheek-like prow blocks; it can fold into a compact helmet-like head unit later. No thin tower neck, no exposed stick-frame torso. Deep structural box beams are inside the shell, seen only through selected recesses. This hull supplies real mass and architectural scale.

BOTTOM LEFT: TWO matching long heavy SUPPORT CARRIERS for the future lower body. In solo mode each is a complete independently propelled armored ship with a long keel, strong broad wedge prow, a thick tapered aft hull, compact engines, retractable landing supports and several massive hinged shell panels. The two ships are recognizably the same design and comparable volume. Their long hull shells later become coordinated armored thighs/shins, with prow armor becoming broad articulated feet and stern landing structures becoming heels. Depict them as handsome long ships now, not preassembled robot legs or freestanding boots. Match the ivory/navy main armor family and use small warm ochre structural accents.

BOTTOM RIGHT: a PAIR of heavy SHOULDER-BOOM assemblies, each folded compactly into its own wedge-shaped propulsion cradle. They are deep boxed beams under broad sloping armor, with thick rotary roots, integrated thrust nozzles, and stout terminal clamp jaws tucked inward along the beam. One is shown fully stowed; the other opens its boom just enough to reveal the hinge and clamp without becoming a robot arm. These will carry large shoulder armor, then rotate forward to grip an opposing cannon cradle during an inverse combination. The boom remains attached to the central chassis while the right propulsion cradle can later release after load transfer. Preserve mass and depth. Avoid thin scaffolding or skeletal girders.

Finish: closely match reference 1 and the adopted source drawings. Sophisticated Japanese mechanical illustration, fine varied linework, large quiet color blocks, dimensional chamfers and heavy plate edges, very dark recessed mechanisms, subtle local metal highlights, restrained maintained paint wear. Mature, monumental, mechanically purposeful and visually elegant. Cream studio background, soft cast shadows. No chibi proportions, toy-plastic gloss, flat infographic shading, uniform thick cartoon outline, neon or photorealistic PBR. Prioritize strong coherent independent ship silhouettes over decorative surface density.

jobs.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: finalized visual proposal for the FIRST 320-meter armored museum giant, in mature Japanese mechanical concept-art style. One imposing full-body hero design, with a small rear three-quarter view occupying at most one quarter of the sheet. The main hero must dominate. No action sequence, no exploded assembly, no labels or diagrams.

Reference roles:
1 is the fleet master sheet. Its upper-left 150-meter museum ship is the exact central ship identity to preserve.
2 is the added ship and armor-module family. Use its heavy armored port shell, matching support carriers and boxed shoulder/propulsion structures as genuine body components. This is the SMALLER, earlier 320-meter frame, not the later 900-meter fleet giant.
3 and 4 establish mature heroic proportions, mechanical depth, painted linework and surface detail. Do NOT copy their colors, head, shoulder towers or chest design wholesale.
5 is the original adopted museum ship: its terraced public galleries, blue glass window bands, glazed dome, orange entrance arch and underlying dark structural hull are the cultural identity. There is exactly ONE museum ship in this robot, not a fleet of miniature museums attached all over it.

Primary silhouette:
A towering complete ARMORED HERO with a recognizable compact helmet/head, broad strong shoulders, substantial chest, controlled narrow waist, coherent pelvis, long powerful coordinated legs and broad articulated wedge feet. Civilian architecture has transformed into a giant, but it is handsome and monumental before any small detail is read. The limbs are muscular armored masses, not exposed cranes or a skeleton. Balanced mature proportions, distinctly tall and long-legged rather than squat. Front three-quarter view from a low camera, standing firmly on enormous offshore harbor support pads. Tiny harbor structures, cranes and pinpoint service workers at the feet establish a 320-meter scale without distracting scenery.

Central museum:
The single 150-meter museum hull has raised its prow and stands VERTICALLY inside the central chest-to-abdomen armor cradle. Its bow points upward. The added frame supplies the rest of the 320-meter body. Most of the museum's structural mass is enclosed by the outer hero armor; small protected openings reveal a short familiar exhibition window strip and the orange entrance arch, and a partial blue glazed gallery from the original ship. These glimpses are inset into the chest, not a huge open display cabinet. The original entrance and window architecture remain readable. Interior floor decks are independently stabilized; do not pretend the museum ship simply grows humanoid limbs. Do not show a second horizontal museum ship anywhere.

Head and upper body:
A handsome compact dark-navy and ivory helmet encloses the short command/observation bridge. Narrow warm illuminated observation windows sit beneath a strong armored brow, with a restrained ivory face shield and short integrated side cheek guards. The head sits directly into a deep neck collar with real armored support. No thin tower neck, no ship bridge perched on a stalk, no antenna crown copied from another robot. Broad two-part sloping shoulder shells close over thick boxed load beams. A sheltered hangar mouth sits under each shoulder. On the robot's anatomical RIGHT shoulder (viewer LEFT) keep a very small distinctive blue repair weld line on a gray/ivory panel. Two staggered-height rear load frames are folded beneath a continuous back armor shell; a rear inset should make that source understandable without exposing a naked ladder frame.

Arms and legs:
Both arms have comparable lengths and mature load-bearing proportions. Long workship hull armor has folded into strong upper-arm and forearm shells; tiny hatch rows, stern thrust blocks and deep circular elbow bearings reveal the vessel origin. Five thick segmented mechanical fingers per hand, each hand a believable built-in articulated ship manipulator, calm fists or relaxed half-open hands. No claw toys, tiny wrists or mismatched thin/huge arms.
Two matching support-carrier hulls unfold into long armored legs. Large ivory shin plates and navy side hulls create a powerful tapered shape, separated by deep mechanical knee and ankle recesses. Wide wedge ship prows become the feet, with short articulated heels and heavy load locks planted in the offshore pads. A few stern engine/nozzle blocks remain visible along the rear calves and hips. Avoid short rectangular boots and exposed stick thighs.

Color and finish:
Dominant ivory and deep navy armor, small carefully placed orange ship-identity blocks, warm tiny windows, a little aged gray and one blue repair mark. The colors form large integrated zones across the entire hero. No random patchwork rainbow, no uniform yellow outlines.
Match the adopted source illustration's fine varied linework, thick armor edges, angled chamfers, deep occluded industrial joints, layered local shadows and subtle paint maintenance wear. Broad calm armor surfaces alternate with concentrated intricate joint mechanisms. This is rich dimensional illustrated mecha concept art, not flat cartoon shading, plastic toy gloss, neon, photographic PBR, or a pile of tiny boats pasted onto a generic robot.
Warm off-white background, grounded soft shadows, main figure fully within frame. No text, numbers, arrows, logos or watermark.

jobs.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: a single monumental full-body hero portrait of WANJIDIAN, the later 900-meter allied fleet giant. This is the COMPLETE NORMAL ARMORED STATE, before inverse combination. No action panels, no exploded view, no cutaway, no repeated miniature robot.

Reference roles:
1 is the independent museum/support fleet master. Preserve those actual ship identities.
2 is the independent gunship/armor/support-carrier/shoulder-boom master. These actual ships and modules become the giant's structure; they do not become decorations pasted onto a generic robot.
3 is the earlier 320-meter museum giant and proves the mature armor/rendering direction. The new 900-meter giant must be DISTINCTLY BROADER, more massive, with different chest layout and later fleet composition, not this same robot scaled up.
4 and 5 define sophisticated Japanese illustrated mechanical depth, coherent heroic masses and subtle wear. Do not copy their heads or shoulder towers.

Main composition and silhouette:
One mighty 900-meter tall orbital armored hero, its SHOULDER SPAN approximately 700 meters. Broad and monumental yet recognizably a complete handsome humanoid: compact helmet, powerful shoulder girdle, substantial closed breast armor, a defined waist and pelvis, long strong fully armored legs and articulated wedge feet. The broad shoulder caps extend outward as enormous sloping armored ship-prow masses, not thin wings or towers. The body has far more width and mass than reference 3, while keeping long legs and a coordinated head-to-body relationship. No tiny stalk neck. No exposed skeletal torso, no short chibi legs.
Front three-quarter low view, both arms readable. The giant moves slowly in orbit with one foot slightly forward, small recessed thrusters working around the body. A subtle pale Earth limb below and a few very small independent ships establish scale. Mostly warm cream/off-white concept-art background, no busy space battle. The entire figure inside the frame.

Critical orientation: the giant's anatomical RIGHT ARM is on the VIEWER'S LEFT side of the picture. It is formed end-to-end from the two gunships in reference 2:
- VIEWER LEFT UPPER ARM is the dark NAVY/IVORY long gun cruiser.
- VIEWER LEFT FOREARM is the distinctly GRAY/DEEP CRIMSON long gun cruiser.
Keep the two hulls visually distinct but mechanically integrated by a thick deep rotary elbow collar. Each gunship's broad armor panels, long axis, tiny bridge/window rows, integrated gun batteries and stern engine features remain traceable in its respective arm segment. They fold/reposition into strong balanced arm armor rather than hanging alongside another ordinary arm. The gray-red ship's protected prow manipulator bay deploys a thick five-finger mechanical hand at the wrist. This is two actual ship bodies, not color patches on a generic arm and not little tugboats with guns.

Anatomical LEFT / VIEWER RIGHT:
The left shoulder is genuinely damaged and lower/less complete, with one outer armor section missing and dark braced structure showing only in that damaged area. The wide ivory-and-blue-green BRIDGE-RESCUE SHIP from reference 1 supports the outside of this wounded shoulder, its substantial coherent hull, buffered tow recesses and propulsion still recognizable. This is Zhanqiao, a real ship capable of leaving later, not a broken scaffold. The left arm remains an intact heavy gray/ivory/navy mechanical arm, coordinated in length and weight with the right. Preserve the asymmetry without making the whole hero look unfinished or flimsy.
The ivory/ochre maintenance cruiser Zhendeng is nested near the VIEWER RIGHT lower chest/waist, with its lower service/pipe arm partly retracted and protected. It stays a credible armored hull; do not turn it into a naked beam.
The dark red/gray folding-wing escort Zhefan remains clearly SEPARATE, flying outside the giant on the VIEWER RIGHT at lower-body height. Its unrepaired coupling is not attached and it carries no neighboring ship's weight. Only this one escort need be visibly detached.

Chest and museum core:
The huge orbital dock carrier from reference 2 supplies continuous large ivory/navy chest and shoulder armor, deep boxed internal structure, inhabited side-dock modules and the central cradle. In resting state the breastplates are CLOSED and handsome. No giant open shelf, no museum-shaped tumor, no exposed skeletal rectangular chest.
There is exactly ONE original 150-meter museum ship, HORIZONTAL deep inside the center of this 900-meter body. Only a small recessed horizontal band of familiar warm-lit blue exhibition windows and a PARTIAL curved blue glass dome are visible through a controlled central armor aperture. It is a small cultural heart within a much larger body, not the entire chest and not a second ship outside. Most of the museum hull is hidden behind the breast armor. Retain a believable side/down exit route as closed seams under the commercial side-dock plates.
Industrial yellow release locks appear sparingly as small recessed latch housings along the side-dock seams. They are mechanical locks, not flower symbols or orange decorations. The broad shoulder boxed beams sit inside large armored shells, ready to rotate forward later but CLOSED now.

Head and lower body:
A compact strong helmet encloses the command bridge, deep navy crown, ivory cheek guards, warm narrow observation visor beneath an armored brow and a protected face shield. Short deep neck collar, integrated head support. No tall bridge tower used as a neck, no copied twin-antenna crown, no bird beak.
The paired long support-carrier hulls supply extensive ivory/navy thigh/shin armor and broad coherent feet. Hull bevels, deep joint recesses and small thruster groups make the ship origins intelligible. Long coordinated legs, distinct knee bearings, real ankle articulation and wide but elegant wedge feet. Exposed mechanisms stay in joints, not across whole limbs. Large armor shapes carry the design.

Finish: sophisticated painted mechanical concept art exactly in the source family: fine varied dark drawing, thick armor edges, dimensional sloping planes, deep occlusion, layered local shadows, tiny human-scale windows and maintenance hatches, subtle maintained paint wear. Ivory/navy dominate; the gray-red right forearm and blue-green support ship are purposeful distinct accents. Preserve calm large color regions. No plastic toy gloss, no flat cartoon simplification, no chunky uniform outline, no neon, no PBR. No text, numbers, arrows, logo or watermark.

jobs.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: a clear FOUR-PANEL mechanical action study of the inverse combination of the EXACT allied giant in reference 1. This is a separate narrative action sheet, not its normal hero portrait. Sophisticated Japanese mechanical illustration, the same mature detailed linework, armor volume, colors and restrained painted finish as the references.

References:
1 = exact 900-meter Wanjidian body to preserve in every panel. Navy upper arm and gray-red forearm are anatomical RIGHT / viewer LEFT; damaged anatomical LEFT shoulder has the ivory/teal bridge-rescue ship Zhanqiao.
2 = the solo ships. TOP LEFT is the single museum ship; TOP RIGHT is Zhanqiao rescue ship; BOTTOM LEFT is Zhendeng maintenance cruiser with pipe arm; BOTTOM RIGHT is Zhefan outboard escort. Never interchange these identities.
3 = the actual armor-dock carrier, right-arm gunships, support carriers and thick shoulder-boom/clamp modules. These are the parts that move.
4 = hostile Tianqiong/cannon reference. In the final panel, show only a cropped section of that ENEMY'S large external gun cradle as the object being gripped; do not change Wanjidian into Tianqiong.

Layout: landscape sheet, four equally clear substantial vignettes in a 2 by 2 reading order, generous cream gutters, NO written labels, numbers, arrows, captions, logos or watermark. Each panel depicts ONE instance of the same allied giant and exactly ONE museum ship, hidden or visible according to the stage. This is four different moments, not four robots in one scene. Keep the same front/side three-quarter orientation and lighting across panels, with a faint Earth limb always toward the LOWER LEFT, so the Earth-side escape direction stays understandable. Do not invert the giant's right-arm colors between panels. The main torso, hips, armored legs and compact head remain continuous throughout; only the specified side-dock/chest covers are released.

TOP LEFT — TAKE THE WEIGHT, BEFORE RELEASE:
The giant is still in its closed-chest normal state from reference 1. Two small but credible independent navy/ivory utility towships have moved to the two ends of the substantial commercial side-dock/chest-cover assembly.
